title: Decision: the agent's VTC capability is opt-in, and the default is revisited when a client exists
description:
Mark decided 2026-11-23, for bead mimid-1wgh.114.2, after decision
mimid-1wgh.118 settled which document the surface extends.

THE QUESTION. The capability hands a client the call room's media secret
(draft-atwood-mimi-calls §4.3). Is it on by default like the rest of the
agent's JMAP front end, or off unless configured?

THE HOUSE STYLE IT IS MEASURED AGAINST: [jmap] is on by default and
loopback only; [irc] is off by default, and takes any address only
because the operator controls exposure (decision mimid-1wgh.92). On by
default when loopback-only and needed for the main job; off when it
widens exposure.

THE ARGUMENT THAT IT CHANGES NOTHING: the agent already serves PLAINTEXT
over this endpoint to anyone holding the local token or an app password
(docs/design/frontend-auth.md §3). That credential already reads every
message the user can read, and a media secret for a room the user is a
member of is something their own device legitimately computes.

THE ARGUMENT THAT IT DOES, which was taken as the stronger: plaintext and
key material leak differently. A client given plaintext can read only
what the agent already decrypted for it. A client given media_secret can
decrypt media the agent never saw, including media captured off the wire
elsewhere, and holds that for the whole epoch. And it goes to EVERY JMAP
client on the machine, including one the user installed for chat and
never thought about for calls.

WHAT ACTUALLY DECIDED IT: nothing implements the extension yet. On by
default today would hand out call keys for a feature no client can use.
Opt-in costs the demo deployment one config line and costs everyone else
nothing.

CHOSEN: opt-in. Off unless configured, and NOT advertised in the Session
object when off, so a client learns not to try rather than being refused
mid-call.

NOT CHOSEN:
- On by default, loopback only. The product argument for it is real --
  mimid exists to serve stock clients and Mark 2026-11-23 called VTC "the
  feature that normies will demand" -- but it is not real YET: nobody
  gets calls by default today whatever is chosen, because no client
  implements the extension.
- A credential of its own, an app password scoped to calls rather than
  the general local token. Strongest separation and the right shape if
  this ever needs it, but a new credential concept to design and
  document for a surface with no users.

REVISIT WHEN: a client implements the extension. Then flipping the
default is one line, decided with evidence rather than a guess. This
bead is the record of what the guess would have been.
close_reason: Mark 2026-11-23: opt-in, not advertised when off; revisit the default once a client implements the extension.
